useSyncExternalStore()

The useSyncExternalStore() method connects a React render to the State of a and returns its current immutable Snapshot.

This method is available only for React and extends the contract with a React render-time subscription surface.

React Package

The React extension is available from the /react package on npm. 

{{`npm install @sdux-vault/react`}}

Download /react from npm →

Usage

Use useSyncExternalStore() when a React component renders State. It gives the current render an immutable Snapshot and allows React to render the component again after that State changes.

Choose the State access surface
Surface Usage Result
useSyncExternalStore() Render State in a React component Returns the current Snapshot and connects the render to future State changes.
state Read State outside render Returns the latest Snapshot synchronously without creating a subscription.
state$ Observe every State emission Provides an Observable for consumers that explicitly manage a subscription and its cleanup.
Do not rely on later updates to validate the initial render
  1. Initial render: A React subscription created from state$ after the has initialized can miss the earlier emission that committed initialState. The first render can therefore omit the configured initial State.
  2. Later updates: A subsequent replaceState() or mergeState() emission can reach the subscription and render correctly. This creates a false-positive result: later updates work even though the initial render was not correctly connected.
  3. Merge Behavior: The committed initial State still exists when the UI misses it. An add-on Merge Behavior can combine a later mergeState() value with that initial State, causing both values to appear after the merge even though the initial value was not visible on the first render.
  4. Correct approach: Use useSyncExternalStore() for the render path so React reads the current Snapshot during render and remains connected to subsequent State changes through the same subscription contract.

Before the first render

The must already be initialized by the application's State setup. Import its stable reference into the React component; do not create or initialize it inside the component render.

During render

  1. Call useSyncExternalStore() at the top level of the React function component.
  2. Do not call it conditionally, inside a loop, inside an event handler, or from a regular utility function.
  3. Read hasValue, value, isLoading, and error from the returned Snapshot to determine what the component renders.

After render

React manages the render subscription created by useSyncExternalStore(). When the commits new State, React requests the latest Snapshot and renders the subscribed component again. The component does not need a separate state$ subscription or manual subscription cleanup for this render path.

Event handlers, effects, and non-rendering code

Use state when an event handler or other imperative code needs the latest Snapshot at the moment that code runs. Use state$ for observation outside the React render path when every State emission is required, and always dispose of that Observable subscription when its owner is no longer active.

Render State with one subscription surface

For React UI, use useSyncExternalStore() as the subscription surface. Reading state during render does not connect that render to future State changes, while using state$ creates a separate subscription lifecycle that the component must manage.

Method Contract
Runtime Invocation
Method Description
useSyncExternalStore<T>

inputs:

  • None

return:

  • StateSnapshotShape<T>
Subscribes the current React render to State updates and returns the latest committed Snapshot.
Snapshot Output

The returned Snapshot represents the latest committed State for the .

Example

This component imports an existing, initialized and uses useSyncExternalStore() as its render subscription. Each Snapshot field maps to an explicit UI state, and committed State changes cause React to render the component again with the latest Snapshot. 

{{`export function ExampleView() {
  const snapshot = exampleCell.useSyncExternalStore();

  if (snapshot.isLoading) {
    return <p>Loading...</p>;
  }

  if (snapshot.error) {
    return <p role="alert">{snapshot.error.message}</p>;
  }

  if (!snapshot.hasValue) {
    return <p>No State is available.</p>;
  }

  return <pre>{JSON.stringify(snapshot.value, null, 2)}</pre>;
}`}}
